title: Seniors: UF and FSU deadlines are October 15
subtitle: Your weekly plan for the Class of 2027
body_content:
Hi there,

Senior fall moves fast, and the next three weeks have real deadlines. Here's what matters for the Class of 2027 right now.

This week at a glance

  • Oct 15: UF Early Decision and FSU Early Decision/Early Action deadlines
  • Oct 23: Register for the Nov 7 SAT
  • Now: File the FAFSA, and put Florida's own aid form (the FFAA) on your list

1. Thursday, October 15: UF and FSU

UF Early Decision: UF added a binding Early Decision option this year. The application is due Oct 15, and the self-reported academic record (STARS) is due Oct 22. If your student isn't 100% sure UF is their first choice, skip ED. UF Early Action (non-binding) is due Nov 1, with STARS due Nov 8.

FSU: Both Early Decision (binding) and Early Action (non-binding, Florida residents only) are due Oct 15. Decisions come out Dec 17.

Do this: Sit down with your senior this weekend and confirm which schools they're applying to early and which plan (ED or EA) they're choosing for each.

2. Financial aid: two applications, not one

The 2027–28 FAFSA is open at StudentAid.gov. There's no single "FAFSA deadline" that matters most. Each college sets its own priority date, so check the financial aid page of every school on your student's list.

Florida also has its own form: the Florida Financial Aid Application (FFAA). This is how your student applies for Bright Futures and other state aid. The final deadline is August 31 after graduation, but there's no reason to wait. Knock it out this fall.

3. Last chances to raise a test score

For the Class of 2027, Bright Futures requires an SAT of 1330 (Florida Academic Scholars) or 1190 (Florida Medallion Scholars), plus the GPA and service-hour requirements. If your senior is close, upcoming SAT dates are:

  • Nov 7: register by Oct 23
  • Dec 5: register by Nov 20

Bright Futures accepts test scores from tests taken through August 31 after graduation, but colleges want scores much sooner. Check each school's score deadline.

Term of the week: Early Decision vs. Early Action

Early Decision (ED) is binding: if admitted, your student commits to attend and withdraws every other application. Early Action (EA) is not binding: you apply early, hear back early, and still have until May 1 to decide. When in doubt, choose EA.

Dates and policies can change, so always confirm on each school's official admissions page. Questions? Just hit reply. We read every email.

Talk soon,
The College Plan Team
